subject.title: fix(browser): keep tab reachability retry delay abortable

question: Does the present production-route, real-timer evidence with a mocked reachability probe satisfy the external-PR real-behavior gate for browser tab cancellation, or should this PR provide a real OpenClaw-managed browser mutation run?
rationale: The patch is mechanically small and the supplied output directly measures the intended delay, but repository review policy requires external PRs to show after-fix behavior in a real setup unless a maintainer intentionally accepts a narrower proof boundary.

options.title: Require managed-browser proof
options.body: Ask for a redacted real OpenClaw-managed browser tab close, focus, or select run cancelled during the retry window, including elapsed time and confirmation that no mutation follows.

options.title: Accept route-level proof
options.body: Treat the real-timer production route evidence as sufficient for this isolated delay change and proceed with normal maintainer merge review.

recommendation.title: Require managed-browser proof
recommendation.body: Ask for a redacted real OpenClaw-managed browser tab close, focus, or select run cancelled during the retry window, including elapsed time and confirmation that no mutation follows.

likelyOwner.reason: The PR discussion explicitly asks this reviewer candidate to decide whether the existing proof is sufficient.
